variants.description: Hana translated 月次締め (the monthly closing period) as 'calendar month'. The team built exactly what the English ticket said.

chain.text: Ticket OC-142 says: 'Export rows grouped by calendar month.'
The Japanese spec says 月次締め: the client's monthly closing period, which ends on the 20th.
Hana's translation note says '締め unclear, assumed calendar month, to confirm', but nobody asked the client.

fixes: Change the export to group rows by the client's closing period (21st to 20th) and re-deliver.
Re-run acceptance on the corrected export together with the client's accounting team.
prevention: Keep a glossary of the client's business terms (締め日, 月次) and use it in every spec translation.
A translation marked 'to confirm' blocks its ticket until the client answers.

variants.description: The client asked for the closing period in chat. Linh agreed, but nobody updated the spec or created a ticket.

chain.text: The spec document was last revised before the chat request and still says 'calendar month'.
In the shared chat, the client asked to switch the export to the closing period and Linh replied 'OK, will do'.
No ticket was created for the change, so Minh built the export from the original spec.

fixes: Build the closing-period export the client asked for in chat and re-deliver.
Confirm the final requirement with the client in writing before re-delivery.
prevention: Any change agreed in chat is copied into the spec and a ticket the same day.
Development starts only from a spec revision that lists every agreed change.

variants.description: The team took Tanaka-san's はい as approval of calendar-month grouping. He meant 'I hear you, I will check with accounting'.

chain.text: At the design review, the team proposed grouping the export by calendar month to keep it simple.
The meeting notes record Tanaka-san's reply as 'はい (approved)'.
Tanaka-san meant 'I understand, I will check with accounting'; his follow-up message in the shared chat was never answered.

fixes: Change the export to the closing period the client's accounting team needs and re-deliver.
Walk the client through the corrected export before the next acceptance run.
prevention: After each meeting, confirm decisions in writing with a clear yes/no question.
The BrSE explains indirect replies like はい in the meeting notes instead of recording them as approval.

red_herrings.text: Minh fixed a crash in the export screen two days before the release.
The final regression run finished six hours late because the test server was down.
A timezone setting on the export server was changed on release day.
On the client's PCs, the CSV headers show broken Japanese characters.
